title: Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drains
description: Using a sanitary tee to connect horizontal drainage lines is a common installation mistake that leads to frequent blockages. A sanitary tee has a tight turn designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow, allowing gravity and air venting to function correctly. When installed horizontally, waste lacks the sweeping transition required to maintain velocity, causing solids to settle and clog the line. Model plumbing codes mandate wyes or combination wye-and-eighth bends for horizontal-to-horizontal transitions to ensure smooth flow directional change.

Why Sanitary Tees Fail on Horizontal Drains

Using a sanitary tee to connect horizontal drainage lines is a common installation mistake that leads to frequent blockages. A sanitary tee has a tight turn designed primarily for transitioning from horizontal to vertical flow, allowing gravity and air venting to function correctly. When installed horizontally, waste lacks the sweeping transition required to maintain velocity, causing solids to settle and clog the line. Model plumbing codes mandate wyes or combination wye-and-eighth bends for horizontal-to-horizontal transitions to ensure smooth flow directional change.
